title: The Tallow Works — the rendering house two leagues north-east of Sill
caption: The sheep-fat works known in Sill only by the smell on a north wind, drawn at walking scale: the rendering house or fat-house with its three vats, the hot flue and the thumb-wide warm crack where the wall meets it with grey paper nests hung behind, the lamp-room with its trimmed lamps and the leaf kept under a cracked saucer, the byre where the men sit at the turning of the year, the nest-fire at the shed door with the burnt paper beside it, the sheep-folds on the rise, and the sluice run carrying ash and wash-water away south-east. The ridge road comes in from the north gate past Cold Acre, both drawn faint, and the sweet smoke goes down on a north wind toward Sill. Cartouche dated Y.H. 813, the month of Bone, with compass, a league scale in paces, a convention of signs and surveyor's notes on the fourth cup poured under the bench and the clerk who set it on the floor, the wasp that comes to the warmth and not the fat with twelve nests burnt and no value arising, fever first and the cold after with no figure asked for, the coal that comes up in clay on Kindling and the Long Night's cost, the nought written where a name should stand, and the second warm crack in the cold north wall that has never held a nest and is set down in words but not marked on the wall. An engraved tallow lamp and an engraved tallow-wasp sit in the margin.
